raw.quick_summary: A Future follows a simplified asynchronous lifecycle: it begins pending, may start running, and can successfully finish. A pending Future may instead be cancelled. Finished and cancelled are terminal states; running or finished computations cannot be cancelled in this model.

key_concepts.explanation: An abstraction representing an asynchronous computation.
The initial state of a Future before computation starts. It can transition to running or cancelled.
The state of a Future after it has started computation. Successful completion moves it to finished.
A terminal state reached after successful completion.
A terminal state that may be reached by cancelling a pending Future.
A state from which no further lifecycle transitions occur; finished and cancelled are terminal in this simplified model.
Cancellation may change pending to cancelled, but it cannot cancel a computation that is already running or finished.

learning_path.title: Understanding the Future Lifecycle
learning_path.reason: The lesson can be learned by following the allowed state transitions from initialization through completion or cancellation, then identifying terminal states and restrictions.

steps.title: Begin with the pending state
steps.learning_goal: Identify the initial state of a Future and its possible exits.
steps.explanation: A Future starts in pending. From this state, it may be started and become running, or it may be cancelled and become cancelled.
steps.connection_to_previous: This establishes the starting point for the lifecycle before any transition occurs.

steps.title: Start the computation
steps.learning_goal: Understand the transition from pending to running.
steps.explanation: Starting a pending Future changes its state to running, indicating that the asynchronous computation has begun.
steps.connection_to_previous: Once the initial pending state is known, the next step is the normal start transition.

steps.title: Reach successful completion
steps.learning_goal: Understand how a running Future becomes finished.
steps.explanation: If the running computation completes successfully, the Future changes to finished.
steps.connection_to_previous: The running state is the prerequisite for the successful-completion transition.

steps.title: Handle cancellation and terminal states
steps.learning_goal: Distinguish valid cancellation from terminal states.
steps.explanation: Cancellation can move a pending Future to cancelled, but it cannot cancel a running or finished computation. Both cancelled and finished are terminal states with no further transitions in this simplified model.
steps.connection_to_previous: After understanding normal execution, compare it with the cancellation branch and identify where the lifecycle ends.

checkpoint_questions.question: What state does a pending Future enter when it is started?
checkpoint_questions.explanation: Starting changes the Future from pending to running.

checkpoint_questions.question: Which cancellation transition is valid in the simplified lifecycle?
checkpoint_questions.explanation: Only a pending Future may be changed to cancelled; running and finished computations cannot be cancelled in this model.

checkpoint_questions.question: A Future is running and then completes successfully. What is true afterward?
checkpoint_questions.explanation: Successful completion changes running to finished, and finished is terminal.
